skill.name: error-detective
skill.description: Search logs and codebases for error patterns, stack traces, anomalies, and likely root causes during debugging and production incident investigation.
skill.summary: Analyze logs, stack traces, and error trends to build evidence-based debugging hypotheses.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Production errors are hard to trace across logs, stack traces, and service changes. This skill structures evidence into timelines, correlations, and root cause hypotheses.
actual_capabilities: Extract error patterns from logs with targeted regular expressions.
Analyze stack traces across multiple programming languages.
Correlate errors with deployments, service changes, and time windows.
Identify error rate spikes and anomaly patterns in log streams.
Draft monitoring queries for Elasticsearch, Splunk, and similar tools.
Produce root cause hypotheses with supporting evidence and likely code locations.
limitations: Requires relevant logs, stack traces, metrics, or code context from the user.
Cannot access production systems or observability tools unless the host agent provides access.
Root cause conclusions are hypotheses until validated against runtime evidence.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the scanned file list.

use_cases.title: Investigate incident spikes
use_cases.description: Correlate error spikes with deployments, time windows, and affected services during production incidents.

use_cases.title: Debug stack traces
use_cases.description: Turn stack traces and log snippets into likely failure paths and code locations to inspect.

use_cases.title: Summarize customer-impacting errors
use_cases.description: Group repeated errors and prepare clear evidence for engineering escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Find error patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these log lines and identify repeated error patterns, affected components, and likely next checks.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a stack trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this stack trace. Explain the likely failure path, the most relevant frames, and what code I should inspect first.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate an incident timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these logs, deployment times, and symptoms to build an incident timeline with correlations and evidence-backed hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Design recurrence detection
prompt_templates.prompt: Create monitoring queries and alert conditions that would detect this failure pattern early without excessive noise.

output_examples.input: A payment service shows a sudden increase in timeout errors after a deployment.
output_examples.output: The analysis groups timeout messages by service, builds a timeline around the deployment, and highlights downstream dependency latency as the leading hypothesis.

output_examples.input: A stack trace contains repeated null reference errors from a request handler.
output_examples.output: The result identifies the first application frame, explains the likely missing input state, and lists targeted checks for validation and prevention.

output_examples.input: Several services report different errors during the same fifteen-minute window.
output_examples.output: The output separates primary errors from cascading failures and proposes a correlation plan using timestamps, service boundaries, and deployment events.

best_practices: Provide timestamps, service names, deployment context, and representative log samples.
Ask for evidence ranking when multiple root cause hypotheses are possible.
Validate proposed fixes with recurrence checks and monitoring queries.
anti_patterns: Do not provide isolated error messages without surrounding context or timing.
Do not treat correlation as proof without validating runtime evidence.
Do not apply broad fixes before identifying the first failing component.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide error messages, stack traces, timestamps, affected services, recent changes, and any known customer impact.

faq.question: Can it analyze distributed system failures?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to correlate errors across services, time windows, and deployment events.

faq.question: Does it connect to log platforms directly?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest queries, but direct access depends on the host agent and user permissions.

faq.question: Can it produce monitoring queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft practical queries for tools such as Elasticsearch and Splunk.

faq.question: Will it always find the root cause?
faq.answer: No. It produces evidence-based hypotheses that still need validation against logs, metrics, and system behavior.

faq.question: Is this skill only for production incidents?
faq.answer: No. It is also useful for local debugging, regression analysis, and post-incident prevention planning.
